name: Computer Networks - Foundations & Models
description: Network types, OSI & TCP/IP models, services, protocols, standards bodies, and use cases (CCN01)

questions.question: A company connects employee PCs to a central database server so multiple departments can access shared records. Which network use case best matches this?
options: Home application: broadband access for personal devices
Business application: resource sharing / client-server access
Mobile user application: remote VPN access to company resources
Social networking application: peer-to-peer content sharing

questions.question: A household uses the Internet primarily for video streaming and online gaming. In the book's framing, this is best classified as:
options: Business application
Mobile user application
Home application
Social application

questions.question: A smartwatch synchronizes with a phone over a few meters using very low power. This best fits which network type?
options: LAN
WAN
MAN
PAN

questions.question: An 'internetwork' is best described as:
options: A single enterprise LAN using VLANs to segment departments
A wireless mesh network linking access points across a campus
A collection of interconnected networks that appear as one network to hosts
A high-speed fiber backbone linking geographically distant data centers

questions.question: In networking terminology, a service defines what a layer offers to the layer above, while a protocol defines:
options: The physical medium and signaling standard used for transmission
How peer entities implement that service
The maximum frame size supported at the data link layer
The hierarchical addressing scheme used to identify hosts

questions.question: Which challenge is most characteristic of 'mobile users' compared with fixed home/business users?
options: Significantly higher sustained bandwidth requirements
Greater need for quality-of-service guarantees on the link
Maintaining connectivity while changing point of attachment
Higher susceptibility to collisions in shared media environments

questions.question: Which description best matches a typical LAN?
options: A metro-area fiber ring connecting multiple enterprise campuses
A long-haul network connecting branch offices across countries
A building/campus network with high speed and low delay
A carrier-operated packet-switched network spanning a region

questions.question: Which pairing correctly matches the Internet standards body with its typical output?
options: ISO → RFCs
IEEE → Internet drafts submitted to the IETF
IETF → RFCs
ITU-T → IEEE 802 LAN/MAN standards

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a connection-oriented service from a connectionless service?
options: Connection-oriented services use UDP for lower overhead; connectionless services use TCP
Connection-oriented services forward each packet independently; connectionless services use a fixed path
Connection-oriented services involve setup/state to support orderly delivery; connectionless sends independent messages without prior setup
Connection-oriented services guarantee lower latency because the path is negotiated in advance

questions.question: In the OSI reference model, how many layers are there?
What is the primary purpose of a protocol hierarchy (layered architecture)?
options: To ensure each packet carries a header from every layer for traceability
To reduce complexity by dividing networking functions into well-defined layers
To guarantee that all network vendors implement identical hardware interfaces
To push error detection and correction entirely to the physical layer

questions.question: Which organization is most directly associated with Internet standards such as RFCs?
options: ISO
IEEE
ITU
IETF

questions.question: In the TCP/IP reference model, which layer is responsible for moving packets across multiple networks (routing) as a best-effort service?
options: Transport layer
Application layer
Internet layer
Link layer

questions.question: Which network type is standardized under the IEEE 802.11 family?
options: Ethernet LANs
Wireless LANs (WLANs)
Metropolitan area networks
Cellular mobile networks

questions.question: In a layered network architecture, which statement best captures the role of a protocol?
options: It defines the electrical and mechanical properties of the transmission medium
It describes the set of services a layer advertises to the layer above it
It specifies rules for communication between peer entities at the same layer
It translates between symbolic hostnames and numeric network addresses

questions.question: What was the primary motivation behind the OSI reference model?
options: To provide a streamlined alternative to TCP/IP with fewer protocol layers
Enable vendor-independent standardization so diverse systems could interoperate
To consolidate session and presentation functions into a single unified layer
To define a common routing algorithm for inter-domain traffic on the Internet

questions.question: Which criticism applies specifically to the TCP/IP reference model?
options: Its seven-layer design makes practical implementation overly complex
The protocols were defined before the model, making it a poor general template
Poor distinction between services, interfaces, and protocols
It lacks support for the connection-oriented services required by telephony

questions.question: Which difference most strongly contributed to TCP/IP's success over OSI?
options: A more rigorous theoretical separation of services, interfaces, and protocols
A more compact layer structure that reduced header overhead
Availability of working implementations
Formal endorsement and funding from ISO and ITU member governments

questions.question: Which feature most clearly distinguishes a connection-oriented service from a connectionless one?
options: Guaranteed higher bandwidth reserved along the entire path
Mandatory use of symmetric encryption for the session
Explicit setup and teardown phases
Use of broadcast addressing to reach all potential receivers

questions.question: According to Tanenbaum, which issue appears across multiple layers of the protocol stack?
options: Routing
Multiplexing
Encapsulation
Error control

questions.question: Why does the TCP/IP model have fewer layers than the OSI model?
options: TCP/IP was originally designed for resource-constrained, low-bandwidth links
OSI includes separate session and presentation layers that TCP/IP omits
It combines functions based on practical deployment needs
Both B and C are correct

questions.question: Service primitives are important in layered architectures because:
options: They standardize the electrical signaling characteristics of the physical medium
They specify how layers interact at boundaries without exposing internal implementation
They define the maximum throughput achievable at each protocol layer
They establish shared cryptographic keys between communicating layers
